tour.name: Paracas, Ballestas Islands & Huacachina Oasis Private Day Trip from Lima
tour.subtitle: A long private day on Peru's desert coast with a licensed guide and car: a boat to the Ballestas Islands, the 'poor man's Galápagos', with sea lions, penguins and the Candelabra geoglyph, a seafood lunch in Paracas, a pisco vineyard, and a dune buggy and sandboarding at sunset in the oasis of Huacachina.

tour.overview:
South of Lima, the Pacific coast of Peru is a desert, cooled by the Humboldt current, whose cold, nutrient-rich waters feed an extraordinary abundance of marine life. Off the Paracas peninsula, the Ballestas Islands are home to thousands of sea lions, Humboldt penguins, boobies, pelicans and cormorants. Inland, near the city of Ica, the small oasis of Huacachina lies around a lagoon among some of the highest sand dunes in South America, and the valleys produce pisco, Peru's grape brandy.

This private day takes you from Lima to Paracas and Huacachina and back with a licensed guide and a car. You take the morning boat to the Ballestas, have lunch by the bay, taste pisco and end with a dune buggy ride and sandboarding at sunset.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 16 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Lima
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, car and driver; shared boat to the Ballestas
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: easy to moderate; the buggy ride is bumpy

WHAT YOU SEE
• The Ballestas Islands and the Candelabra.
• The Paracas bay.
• A pisco bodega.
• The Huacachina oasis and dunes.

WHY THIS WORKS
A private car makes this long day comfortable, with the freedom to stop, and avoids the fixed schedules of the tourist buses.

WHO IT SUITS
Wildlife lovers, families and adventurous travellers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
With more time, stay a night in Paracas or Huacachina and add a flight over the Nazca Lines.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
The drive is about 3 hours 30 minutes each way. Ballestas boats can be cancelled when the sea is rough. Landing on the islands is not allowed; you see the wildlife from the boat.

days.name: The Ballestas Islands, lunch in Paracas, a pisco bodega and the Huacachina dunes at sunset
days.description:
What to expect: the wildlife and desert of Peru's south coast, with a licensed guide, private car, boat, lunch, tasting and dune buggy.

Your guide and driver collect you at your hotel at about 4:00 and drive south on the Pan-American Highway along the desert coast, about 3 hours 30 minutes, to the port of El Chaco in Paracas. You board the boat for the Ballestas Islands. On the way you pass the Candelabra, a geoglyph 180 metres tall cut into the sandy hillside of the peninsula, whose origin and age are still debated. Around the rocky islands, with their natural arches and caves, thousands of birds – boobies, cormorants, pelicans and Inca terns – cover the cliffs, sea lions bask and bark on the beaches, and Humboldt penguins waddle along the ledges. You also see the guano workers' buildings, as the islands' bird droppings were a precious fertiliser in the 19th century.

Back on land, you have a seafood lunch by the bay of Paracas. You then drive inland to Ica, where you visit a traditional bodega, see the clay jars used for fermenting grape juice and taste several piscos. Your last stop is Huacachina, a small oasis of palm trees around a green lagoon, surrounded by dunes up to 100 metres high. You climb into a dune buggy for a roller-coaster ride over the sand, stopping at the top of the dunes to slide down on sandboards, and watch the sun set over the desert. You drive back to Lima, arriving at about 21:00.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
04:00 – Pick-up at your hotel in Lima.
08:00 – Boat to the Ballestas Islands (about 2 hours).
10:30 – Paracas bay.
12:00 – Seafood lunch.
13:30 – Drive to Ica and pisco bodega.
15:30 – Huacachina oasis.
16:30 – Dune buggy and sandboarding.
18:00 – Sunset and drive back to Lima.
21:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• A flight over the Nazca Lines can be added with a night in Ica or Nazca.
• The Paracas National Reserve, with its red beach and desert cliffs, can replace the bodega.
• Boats depart in the morning only, as the sea gets rough in the afternoon.

INCLUDED: private car and driver, licensed guide, Ballestas boat and fees, lunch, pisco tasting, dune buggy and sandboard, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: Nazca flight, dinner, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Is it a long day?
faq.answer: Yes, about 16 hours with 7 hours of driving. We recommend a night in Paracas or Huacachina if you can.

faq.question: Is the Ballestas boat private?
faq.answer: The boats are shared with other visitors, as private boats are limited by the reserve. Your guide and car are private.

faq.question: What happens if the sea is rough?
faq.answer: If the port authority cancels the boats, we visit the Paracas National Reserve instead.

faq.question: Is the dune buggy safe?
faq.answer: The buggies are driven by experienced local drivers with seat belts; the ride is bumpy and thrilling. Sandboarding is done lying down or standing, as you prefer.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: Yes, a seafood lunch in Paracas. Other dishes are available.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes. Children love the sea lions and the dunes. Child seats are provided free of charge on request.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The boat needs a step down, and the dune buggy is very bumpy.

faq.question: Can we add the Nazca Lines?
faq.answer: Yes, with an overnight stay: flights leave from Pisco, Ica or Nazca in the morning.

faq.question: Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tips are appreciated in Peru but never required.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Layers, a windproof jacket for the boat, a hat, sunglasses, sun cream and closed shoes for the sand.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
faq.answer: All year. December to March is hot and sunny; the sea is calmest in the mornings.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
